- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or trending negative (sentiment < 0.4) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to overshoot in early days of a new trend — adjust downward by 3–8% for the first 3–5 days of a new sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast volatility — smooth out sharp peaks and troughs by 1–2% per swing.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 5–7 days.
- Avoid overreacting to recent high sentiment — if sentiment is high but price is falling, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid lagged overcorrection.
